articles.title: Pickaxe Mountain revives the Kahuta question: Could India have hit Pakistan’s nuclear leap?
articles.content: The West Asia conflict highlights Iran’s nuclear ambitions and US-Israeli efforts to block them. Pickaxe Mountain, housing hidden nuclear facilities, has become a focal point. Strikes on Natanz in 2025 echoed earlier pre-emptive attacks on nuclear programmes worldwide, from Allied raids on Germany’s heavy-water plant in WWII to Israel’s operations against Iraq’s Osiraq reactor (1981) and Syria’s al-Kibar site (2007). India, however, refrained from striking Pakistan’s Kahuta facility in the 1980s, a decision that enabled Pakistan’s nuclearisation. To avoid escalation, India and Pakistan signed a 1988 accord prohibiting attacks on nuclear sites. India now prioritises survivability through layered missile defence projects.

articles.title: How Oracle's 14-year-old legal loss is forcing Microsoft to UK Supreme Court
articles.content: Microsoft is seeking permission to appeal to the UK Supreme Court after losing a £270 million case brought by software reseller ValueLicensing. The Competition Appeal Tribunal ruled in 2025 that reselling Microsoft's perpetual on-premise licences was not copyright infringement, and the Court of Appeal agreed on July 7. Judges said Microsoft's argument echoed the 2012 UsedSoft ruling that went against Oracle. A partial stay means disclosure applications still proceed, with a hearing expected in September.

articles.title: CWG: Why India's fastest man Gurindervir crashed out despite finishing 2nd in heat
articles.content: India's fastest man Gurindervir Singh crashed out of the Commonwealth Games men's 100m heats despite finishing second after clocking 10.39 seconds, with coach James Hillier later revealing he had been carrying a hamstring injury for a month. The 24-year-old, who set a national record of 10.09 seconds in May, finished 28th overall and missed the semifinals.

articles.title: The Harbhajan Singh hand behind Saransh Jain's India breakthrough
articles.content: At 33, with a wealth of domestic cricket experience behind him, Madhya Pradesh off-spinner Saransh Jain on Tuesday earned his maiden India call-up. Jain impressed former India off-spinner Harbhajan Singh during a five-day camp at the BCCI Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Bengaluru, where he caught the legend's eye. Four months later, the off-spinner will board a flight to Sri Lanka for the two-match Test series, starting on August 15 in Galle.

articles.content: Manjot Kalra remains in Sri Lankan custody after a court rejected his bail plea. Investigators are pursuing a high-profile corruption probe linked to the Lanka Premier League. The controversy has also led to the termination of the Jaffna Kings franchise ownership.

articles.content: Microsoft's $190 billion AI capex year isn't buying enough compute, and executives are asking why CEO Satya Nadella's allocation puts Azure tenants like Adobe ahead of M365 Copilot. Business Insider reports Microsoft is now shopping Amazon and Google for capacity after GitHub outages, with the stock down 24% before  Q4 earnings.
